land.text: the duchy's office 'had been fully subsumed into the office of the king'

successors.note: Hohenstaufen page: the duchy of Swabia was subsumed into the kingship; the pages do not name heirs of the ducal lands. Rudolf of Habsburg tried to revive the ducal title in 1273 for his youngest son (infobox 1289-1313).

land.text: Conradin pledged his Swabian inheritance to Ulrich II, count of Wurttemberg

successors.note: A pledge of 1266, not a transfer in 1268; the Duchy of Swabia infobox lists the County of Wurttemberg, the Margraviate of Baden, the Old Swiss Confederacy, the Duchy of Burgundy, the County of Zollern and the Principality of Furstenberg as successors. Needs a dossier.

capitals.name: Hohenstaufen Castle (family seat, near Goppingen)
capitals.note: The family took its name from the castle; the pages give no capital (Duchy of Swabia infobox 'Capital: None'). Coordinates approximate, not from a page.

rulers.name: Conradin
rulers.title: Duke of Swabia (last Hohenstaufen duke)
rulers.note: Executed at Naples in 1268. The pages do not date the start of his ducal tenure; 1260 is Cliopatria's first year.

correction.text: the same shape, valid 1260-1268 only: the duchy 'persisted until 1268, ending with the execution of the last Hohenstaufen duke Conradin'

keyframe_review.note: 50,823 km2 at 7.1-10.5E, 46.2-49.1N (southwest Germany, northern Switzerland, Alsace): Swabia. Cliopatria runs it to 1271; both pages end the Hohenstaufen duchy in 1268 ('The duchy fell into abeyance after Conradin's death in 1268'), so 1269-1271 are not Hohenstaufen land. The infobox extent, 'from the Alsatian Vosges mountain range in the west to the right bank of the river Lech in the east' and south to 'Chiavenna (Kleven) and Gotthard Pass', is wider than the shape east and south; neither page gives an area, so no ratio can be taken. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1260..1268 from this entry's own 'valid 1260-1268 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

region.text: the Duchy of Swabia, held by the Hohenstaufen from 1079

ledger.note: 1260: the last Hohenstaufen hold the Duchy of Swabia. The Hohenstaufen 'held it, with a brief interruption, from 1079 until 1268' (Duchy of Swabia); 'after Conrad's death in 1254, the Great Interregnum followed' (Hohenstaufen). Cliopatria's row begins in 1260; the dynasty's founding in 1079 is the page's, and the page does not date Conradin's ducal tenure.

region.text: The remaining duchy persisted until 1268, ending with the execution of the last Hohenstaufen duke Conradin

ledger.note: 1268: Conradin is executed at Naples and the Hohenstaufen duchy ends. 'The duchy fell into abeyance after Conradin's death in 1268'; the Hohenstaufen page has Charles of Anjou, after Conradin's 1268 defeat at Tagliacozzo, 'publicly executed at Naples'. The office of duke was 'fully subsumed into the office of the king'. In 1266 Conradin had pledged his Swabian inheritance to Ulrich II of Wurttemberg when setting out for Sicily.

wars.name: Conradin's campaign against Charles of Anjou (Tagliacozzo)
wars.outcome: Conradin is defeated at Tagliacozzo in 1268 and executed at Naples; the direct line of the dukes of Swabia ceases. Manfred had been killed at Benevento on 26 February 1266.
wars.note: Fought in Italy; no border of the Swabian shape moves. The Duchy of Swabia page has Conradin 'setting out in 1266 to take possession of Sicily', which is the start year used; neither page gives a month for the invasion or for Tagliacozzo.

certainty.note: A ducal territory with no surveyed edge on either page; the Alsatian, Lech and Alpine limits are approximate.

sources.title: Hohenstaufen
sources.note: Founding 1079, kings and emperors 1138-1254, Conradin executed at Naples after Tagliacozzo (1268), the Interregnum, the duchy subsumed into the kingship. No area, no capital.

sources.title: Duchy of Swabia
sources.note: Hohenstaufen dukes 1079-1268, the pledge of the Swabian inheritance to Ulrich II of Wurttemberg (1266), the duchy in abeyance after 1268, the revived title 1273-1313, the extent of the duchy. No area.

notes: Cliopatria's single Hohenstaufen shape (1260-1271) is the Duchy of Swabia. Both pages end the Hohenstaufen duchy in 1268, so the dossier ends in 1268 and the shape is marked adjust for 1269-1271 (three years that Cliopatria leaves to the Hohenstaufen). The pages do not say who took the ducal lands; successors are the royal domain (the office subsumed into the kingship) and, as a pledge of 1266, the County of Wurttemberg, which needs a dossier (eu-09-x). The House of Habsburg dossier covers the revived ducal title of 1273-1313 only as a title. No infobox area on either page. Page budget: 2 pages, none failed. Coordinates of the castle are approximate and not from a page. Names used that the gazetteer may lack: none beyond region 'Wurttemberg' (present).
